title: SPLIT SECOND
summary: A bowler's approach is cut away from twice before his hand opens. The third time it opens, the ball goes and the pins fall. Dives, a tower fall and a demolition follow, phase by phase. A woman stays on a board. A cloth is put down.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: inconclusive, leaning reference stronger. The sheet is only 42s against a 52s brief. I cannot hear the film, so contact sounds are unjudged.

Noticed before the brief: the bowler's back view recurs at 0-1s, 4-5s, 9-11s and 12-13s. He swings and releases at 5s and 10-11s, with cutaways to the pool diver at 2-3s and the tower diver at 6-8s. This reads as a graphic-match rhythm. The 12-13s frames show the pins and the bowler standing apart, so the pin crash never arrives. At 14-29s dives and splashes (23-25s) run together as one undifferentiated flight-and-splash stretch.

Largest gap: no readable release-to-consequence structure. The brief asks for six bounded excerpts with clear outcomes. The sheet shows two cutaways to the bowler, then a long unrelated run of dives. The woman on the board (30-38s) is a nine-second static hold with no action. The ending is a hand folding cloth at 39-41s, with only garbled ASR over hiss ("the line is on the line" loops), so that line is likely false. I cannot see a consequence that changes this release's weight.

Repairs:
1. Cut the 30-38s hold to at most 3s, or add a release within it. Check: no frame is held static for more than 3s.
2. Show the pins falling after the 10-11s release, at 12-13s. Check: pin motion is visible within 2s of release.
3. Reorder so the 14-25s dives repeat the pattern with a visible cut-away before the release. Check: each cut-away lands before the foot leaves the board.

Strength to protect: the bowler/pool/tower alternation at 0-11s. It is legible and rhythmic.
reviews.builder_note: True that the pins never arrived. A pin-fall shot from the same bowling film was added, with crash sound from a different one (recorded in the ledger), and the board hold was cut from 8.8 s to 5.5 s.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: reference stronger (fails the brief as it stands on the sheet).

Noticed before the brief: the bowler seen from behind recurs at 0-1, 4-5, 9-11. At 5-6 and 10-11 he is already mid-release or past it, so the film cuts to the pole climber or the diver on the beat. At 12-13 the pins are already down. Pool shots at 2-3 interrupt the bowler. This reads as a rhythmic cutaway pattern, not a first-time consequence.

Largest gap: the film has no visible release/consequence structure past about 13s. 14-24 is a long run of diver and fall footage with a blurred whip at 22. Then comes a demolition at 23-24 and a spray at 25-28. Those are loosely related falls, not hands letting go. The woman on the board holds a static pose for 6 seconds (29-34). That is stasis, not an earned hesitation, and the sheet shows no phase alignment. The napkin ending at 35-38 is barely an object transfer, and there are no readable hands. The sheet runs 38.6s, not the 50s the brief asked for. I cannot hear contact sounds. The 6-34s loudness sits at -34 to -38 dB, which suggests hiss. The speech text is probably hiss artifacts.

Repairs:
1. Cut 5-6 and 10-11 to before the bowler's hand opens, so the third return (9-13) shows release then pins. Check: no frame of the bowler's arm past the hand-open in the first two returns.
2. Trim the 29-34 hold to at most 2s or insert action. Check: a visible motion begins before 31s.
3. Put a hand release and a hand transfer, such as the napkin, directly before 35. Check: hand contact is visible within the 35-38s shot.

Protect: the bowler return and the pin-fall payoff at 12-13.
reviews.builder_note: The pins the critic saw at 12-13 s are the shot added after round 1. The second cutaway was trimmed to before the hand opens after this round. The long run of falls and the napkin ending stand as objections.

worked: A bowling instruction film (Let's Go Bowling, Part II, 1955) has a clean approach and release that can be cut at exact phases; the cutaways land on the backswing so the viewer waits for the release.
The consequence sound (pins) comes from a different bowling film (Our Community, 1952), moved on purpose and recorded in the ledger.
failed: The first search sheets for this film failed to load the same way (request-limit errors). The filmstrips for the bowling film and the dives did load and were used. After the cut I checked all twelve reasons against frames and none needed changing.
After the pins the film is a run of falls rather than hands letting go; the dive, tower and fire material is not phase-aligned with the bowler's hand.
The woman on the board is still a static hold; the napkin ending is not a hand release with visible hands.
open: Hand-release and hand-transfer shots before the ending.
Contact sounds are unjudged because I cannot hear.
